statement: The lattice mass-calibration constant C is identical to all digits on every resolution of the dx ladder (dx = 0.02 -> 0.0025, spread exactly 0.0), and at h/dx = 1 the residual mass bias is -2.75e-5 on the tension side, where the Tait equation clamps it to p = 0. The bias is therefore a property of the lattice geometry, not a discretisation error that shrinks with dx: one calibration per lattice suffices.

scope.system: tensorsph.threed lattice calibration + Tait equation of state
exclusions: does not cover disordered particle packing

notes: Practical consequence: resolution studies must not re-tune C, or the ladder measures the calibration, not the scheme.
